issues.legal_issue: The magistrate designated to assist a secured creditor in taking possession of secured assets under the statutory enforcement scheme is not a persona designata.
material_facts: A secured creditor sought assistance from a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate to obtain physical possession of secured assets after the borrower refused to hand over possession.

The governing scheme requires the magistrate to verify the prescribed application formalities and, once satisfied, facilitate possession and forward the assets and related documents to the secured creditor.
The magistrate’s role in this process is ministerial and does not involve adjudicating disputes raised by the borrower against the secured creditor.
The scheme provides time limits for dealing with possession-assistance applications, and the record before the High Court showed substantial numbers of such applications pending.
issues.conclusion: The District Magistrate and Chief Metropolitan Magistrate exercising these powers are not persona designata.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14 of the SARFAESI Act, including its requirements for the secured creditor’s application and affidavit, its time limits, and subsections (1A) and (2), establishes a ministerial process to assist in taking possession rather than an adjudicatory proceeding. The Court relied on NKGSB Cooperative Bank Ltd. v. Subir Chakravarty & Ors. (2022), which characterized the possession-taking step as ministerial and recognized the ability to use an authorized officer to carry it out.

predicates.secured_asset_possession_assistance_case: A secured creditor seeks official assistance to obtain possession of secured assets for enforcement of its security interest.
predicates.magistrate_role_is_limited_to_verifying_: The magistrate verifies the required formalities and facilitates possession without adjudicating disputes between the borrower and the secured creditor.
predicates.magistrate_office_is_not_persona_designa: The statutory function is attached to the relevant office and is not confined personally to the named officeholder.

issues.definition: When a secured creditor seeks possession assistance and the magistrate’s role is limited to checking requirements and facilitating possession, the function is attached to the office rather than personally to its named holder.

issues.legal_issue: An Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or Additional District Magistrate may exercise the possession-assistance powers when the applicable statutory and administrative arrangements place those powers within that magistrate’s authority.
material_facts: The High Court held that Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrates and Additional District Magistrates could exercise the possession-assistance powers, and the borrower challenged that conclusion.
An Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate may be given all or any of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s powers under the Code of Criminal Procedure or another law in force.

The Code of Criminal Procedure places the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate under the Sessions Judge and provides for the allocation of business to an Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate.
Additional District Magistrates may exercise the same relevant powers as District Magistrates where those powers have been conferred by delegation or special order.
The possession-assistance function is ministerial, and the statutory scheme calls for expeditious disposal of applications.
issues.conclusion: The powers may be exercised by the Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate having jurisdiction and by an Additional District Magistrate who exercises the same powers as the relevant District Magistrate through delegation or special order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14 of the SARFAESI Act makes the possession-assistance function ministerial. Under Section 17(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, an Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate may be given the powers of a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate under that Code or another law; Section 19 places both under the Sessions Judge. The Court applied the purposive interpretation that supports expeditious performance of this ministerial function and relied on NKGSB Cooperative Bank Ltd. v. Subir Chakravarty & Ors. (2022) concerning the ministerial character of the function and the use of authorized officers. For an Additional District Magistrate, the Court relied on the fact that the same powers may be exercised through delegation or special order.

predicates.secured_asset_possession_assistance_case: A secured creditor seeks official assistance to obtain possession of secured assets for enforcement of its security interest.
predicates.possession_assistance_role_is_ministeria: The magistrate’s task is to verify the required formalities and facilitate possession rather than adjudicate a dispute.
predicates.additional_chief_magistrate_has_equivale: An Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate has been given the relevant powers of a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate.
predicates.additional_district_magistrate_has_deleg: An Additional District Magistrate has been empowered by delegation or special order to exercise the relevant powers of the District Magistrate.
predicates.qualified_additional_magistrate_may_exer: An Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate with the relevant powers, or an Additional District Magistrate so empowered, may perform the possession-assistance function.

issues.definition: In a possession-assistance case involving a ministerial function, an Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate with equivalent powers or an Additional District Magistrate empowered to exercise the relevant powers may perform that function.
